title: OSHA construction scaffolds practice questions
description: Free practice questions on OSHA scaffold rules (29 CFR 1926 Subpart L). Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: A scaffold's maximum intended load and its rated capacity are different figures. Which one sets the limit on how heavily it may be loaded?

options.A: Whichever of the two is less
options.B: Whichever of the two is greater
options.C: The rated capacity, in every case
options.D: The maximum intended load plus 25 percent

questions.explanation: "Scaffolds and scaffold components shall not be loaded in excess of their maximum intended loads or rated capacities, whichever is less."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The stall load of a scaffold hoist may not exceed how many times the hoist's rated load?

options.A: 6 times
options.B: 3 times
options.C: 10 times
options.D: 8 times

questions.explanation: "The stall load of any scaffold hoist shall not exceed 3 times its rated load."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A qualified person has designed a scaffold. A foreman wants to put more load on it than the design allows because the planks look sturdy. What does the rule require?

options.A: Extra load is allowed if a competent person approves it
options.B: Extra load is allowed for one work shift
options.C: The scaffold must be constructed and loaded in accordance with that design
options.D: The design governs erection only, not loading

questions.explanation: "Scaffolds shall be designed by a qualified person and shall be constructed and loaded in accordance with that design."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Subpart L's definition, what does a scaffold's "maximum intended load" take in?

options.A: The weight of the workers only
options.B: The weight of stored materials only
options.C: The scaffold's own weight multiplied by four
options.D: The total of all persons, equipment, tools, materials, transmitted loads and other loads reasonably anticipated at any one time

questions.explanation: Maximum intended load "means the total load of all persons, equipment, tools, materials, transmitted loads, and other loads reasonably anticipated to be applied to a scaffold or scaffold component at any one time."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.450, Scope, application and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Unless the employer can show a wider space is necessary, what is the widest gap allowed between adjacent platform units on a fully planked platform?

options.A: 1 inch
options.B: 4 inches
options.C: 6 inches
options.D: 12 inches

questions.explanation: Platform units must be installed so the space between adjacent units and between the platform and the uprights "is no more than 1 inch (2.5 cm) wide, except where the employer can demonstrate that a wider space is necessary."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Platforms are overlapped to create a long scaffold platform. Where may the overlap occur?

options.A: Anywhere along the span
options.B: Only over supports
options.C: Only at midspan between supports
options.D: Only at the two ends of the scaffold

questions.explanation: "On scaffolds where platforms are overlapped to create a long platform, the overlap shall occur only over supports," with a minimum overlap unless the platforms are nailed together or otherwise restrained.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does the rule say about covering wood scaffold platforms with opaque finishes?

options.A: Opaque paint is allowed on the whole surface if it is slip-resistant
options.B: Every wood platform must be painted with an opaque finish
options.C: They shall not be covered with opaque finishes, except that platform edges may be covered or marked for identification
options.D: Opaque finishes are allowed on the top surface only

questions.explanation: "Wood platforms shall not be covered with opaque finishes, except that platform edges may be covered or marked for identification."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When may a fork-lift be used to support a scaffold platform?

options.A: Whenever the fork-lift's wheels are chocked
options.B: Whenever the platform simply rests on the forks and the ground is level
options.C: Whenever the employees on the platform wear harnesses
options.D: Only when the entire platform is attached to the fork and the fork-lift is not moved horizontally while the platform is occupied

questions.explanation: "Fork-lifts shall not be used to support scaffold platforms unless the entire platform is attached to the fork and the fork-lift is not moved horizontally while the platform is occupied."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What must the poles, legs, posts, frames and uprights of a supported scaffold bear on?

options.A: Unstable objects, if they are level
options.B: Any object at hand
options.C: Base plates and mud sills or other adequate firm foundation
options.D: Bare soil only

questions.explanation: They "shall bear on base plates and mud sills or other adequate firm foundation," and unstable objects may not be used to support scaffolds.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee wants to step directly between a scaffold and an adjacent surface instead of using a ladder or stair. Direct access is allowed only when the scaffold is no farther from that surface than what?

options.A: 24 inches horizontally and 36 inches vertically
options.B: 14 inches horizontally and 24 inches vertically
options.C: 36 inches horizontally and 48 inches vertically
options.D: 48 inches horizontally and 6 feet vertically

questions.explanation: "Direct access to or from another surface shall be used only when the scaffold is not more than 14 inches (36 cm) horizontally and not more than 24 inches (61 cm) vertically from the other surface."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When is crossbracing acceptable in place of a midrail?

options.A: When the crossing point of two braces is between 20 and 30 inches above the work platform
options.B: At any height, as long as the braces are steel
options.C: When the crossing point is more than 48 inches above the work platform
options.D: When the braces are also used as the means of access

questions.explanation: Crossbracing may replace a midrail "when the crossing point of two braces is between 20 inches (0.5 m) and 30 inches (0.8 m) above the work platform." Separately, "Crossbraces shall not be used as a means of access."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How high above the scaffold supporting level may the bottom rung of a hook-on or attachable ladder be?

options.A: No more than 48 inches
options.B: No more than 36 inches
options.C: No more than 30 inches
options.D: No more than 24 inches

questions.explanation: Hook-on and attachable ladders must be positioned "so that their bottom rung is not more than 24 inches (61 cm) above the scaffold supporting level."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A scaffold part is found damaged so that its strength is below what the rule requires. What must happen to it?

options.A: It must be immediately repaired or replaced, braced to meet the requirements, or removed from service until repaired
options.B: It may stay in use until the job is finished
options.C: It may stay in use if a warning sign is attached
options.D: It must be reported at the next monthly safety meeting

questions.explanation: "Any part of a scaffold damaged or weakened such that its strength is less than that required by paragraph (a) of this section shall be immediately repaired or replaced, braced to meet those provisions, or removed from service until repaired."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A scaffold is covered with ice. When may employees work on it?

options.A: Whenever they wear slip-resistant boots
options.B: Only as necessary to remove the ice
options.C: Whenever a competent person is on site
options.D: Whenever the ice covers less than half the platform

questions.explanation: "Employees shall be prohibited from working on scaffolds covered with snow, ice, or other slippery material except as necessary for removal of such materials."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Scaffold work must be done closer to a power line than the clearance table allows. What must happen before that work proceeds?

options.A: A competent person must watch the line during the work
options.B: Employees on the scaffold must wear rubber gloves
options.C: The utility company or electrical system operator must be notified and must deenergize the lines, relocate them, or install protective coverings
options.D: A warning sign must be posted at the scaffold base

questions.explanation: Closer work is allowed "only after the utility company, or electrical system operator, has been notified of the need to work closer and the utility company, or electrical system operator, has deenergized the lines, relocated the lines, or installed protective coverings to prevent accidental contact with the lines."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee works on a crawling board (chicken ladder). Which of these is listed as acceptable fall protection for that employee?

options.A: A warning line system
options.B: A safety monitoring system
options.C: A controlled access zone
options.D: A three-fourth inch diameter grabline or equivalent handhold securely fastened beside each crawling board

questions.explanation: Each employee on a crawling board "shall be protected by a personal fall arrest system, a guardrail system (with minimum 200 pound toprail capacity), or by a three-fourth inch (1.9 cm) diameter grabline or equivalent handhold securely fastened beside each crawling board."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What fall protection is required for each employee on a single-point or two-point adjustable suspension scaffold?

options.A: Both a personal fall arrest system and a guardrail system
options.B: A guardrail system alone
options.C: A safety net alone
options.D: A grabline alone

questions.explanation: Each such employee "shall be protected by both a personal fall arrest system and guardrail system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Manila or synthetic rope is being used as the toprails and midrails of a scaffold guardrail. What does the rule require?

options.A: Rope may never be used for toprails or midrails
options.B: A competent person must inspect it as frequently as necessary to ensure it continues to meet the strength requirements
options.C: It must be replaced every 30 days
options.D: It needs inspection only when first installed

questions.explanation: "Manila or plastic (or other synthetic) rope being used for toprails or midrails shall be inspected by a competent person as frequently as necessary to ensure that it continues to meet the strength requirements" of the rule.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Besides hardhats, which of these is listed as a way to protect employees on a scaffold from falling hand tools, debris and other small objects?

options.A: Warning signs at the scaffold base
options.B: A safety monitor on the platform
options.C: Debris nets, catch platforms, or canopy structures that contain or deflect the falling objects
options.D: Body belts worn by the employees below

questions.explanation: Additional protection may come from "toeboards, screens, or guardrail systems, or through the erection of debris nets, catch platforms, or canopy structures that contain or deflect the falling objects."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these is listed as a situation in which an employer must retrain a scaffold worker?

options.A: Every six months, whatever the employee's performance
options.B: Whenever the weather changes
options.C: Whenever the employee moves to a new crew on the same site
options.D: Inadequacies in the employee's work involving scaffolds show the employee has not retained the requisite proficiency

questions.explanation: Retraining is required in situations including "Where inadequacies in an affected employee's work involving scaffolds indicate that the employee has not retained the requisite proficiency."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.454, Training requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)
